title: Deeper evidence challenges apparent safeguard leaders

summary.text: INFERENCE: Japan is a defensible next authority-and-cost validation candidate, not an established safety winner; preserve Brazil-first and matched-LUMI-first dissent.
FACT/INFERENCE: E2E commercial continuation separates public-support withdrawal from a service stop; test both switches and actual settlement.
AUDIT RESULT: Production is a 2D plot; only an added preference function supplies ranks. No robust baseline-box dominance supports a general national-versus-coalition conclusion.

SYNTHESIS JUDGMENT: The lenses add operational test refinements to an already strong baseline, not new retrieval or measured panel superiority. Subsequent same-family source review checked 18 external source records plus the local model; it did not review every source or rerun the lenses.

POST-CHECK QUALIFICATION (SC-01/SC-02): Malaysia I8 requires an authorised determination reconciling the broad section6.1 DPIA trigger with section7.1 legal/significant effects and section10.1 AI-used-for-ADMP scope; section10.2 remains best-practices wording. LUMI 2026-02-10 is a last-change date, not an established publication day.

recommendation.decision: First test Japan’s exact authority, amendability, meaningful exposure and marginal cost; enroll one version/fallback experiment only if those gates pass.
recommendation.not: Policy adoption, a global country ranking or a majority vote
recommendation.reversal: Prefer Brazil when a current accessible failed-assurance case offers the more consequential correction test; prefer matched LUMI when delegated shared authority and distinct workload can be exercised. If none qualifies, report unresolved feasibility.

findings.title: The chart supplies hypotheses, not an overall winner
findings.body: AUDIT RESULT: Production is a 2D editorial plot. Only the extra U=.5x+.5y preference yields Japan/Switzerland tied first, Singapore third and India fourth. Six baseline non-dominated routes include EuroHPC and Anthropic. Fifteen regime/prior combinations contain 45 alpha evaluations and 5,760 one-at-a-time probes; three separate removal probes also ran. No dominance relation survives all independent baseline sensitivity boxes. INFERENCE: neither country superiority nor a causal coordination penalty is established; no score update follows.
sourceLocators: model-audit.json: baseline; summary; scenarios; ablations; definitions. Reproduced in memory without writes.

findings.title: Japan has a concrete release boundary, with unproved additionality
findings.body: FACT: Gen-nai requires authorised approval and another developer review, not external independence. DS-920 gives independent testing examples and risk-specific contracting guidance, not a universal signed certificate. ATTRIBUTED POSITIONS: Graffer/Rakuten identify unavailable upstream evidence; government allows reasonable negotiated disclosure but retains demanding change-control expectations. INFERENCE: validate an actual behavioural hold, useful fallback and benefit beyond fully compliant ordinary controls before adding a mandatory layer.

findings.title: India has separate funding and service switches
findings.body: FACT: One provider, E2E, documents commercial continuation after project expiry and service/SKU-specific accounting. Policy assigns roles, logging and revocable access, but an executed safety-specific flow-down and settlement join remain missing. INFERENCE: a subsidy hold cannot automatically be called a workload stop. Ordinary expiry is not observed safety evasion. Separate post-tuning testing, applicant burden and prospective support decisions from retrospective payment cancellation.
sourceLocators: E2E: Billing, Platform Service, Multiple IndiaAI Projects
Qi: abstract only; not current system failure rates

findings.title: LUMI offers a shared implementation hypothesis, not shared consent
findings.body: FACT: CSC is the common contracting surface; supplementary terms and common utilisation rules exist, with purpose-limited content access and retained user IP. INFERENCE: a lawfully delegated host annex could avoid repeated national rewrites. Exact delegation, rights, willing projects, cost and additional metered activity remain unproved. Belgian scope nests in national scope; neither allocation share is protected consumption. Host controls cannot recall exported weights or prevent off-host migration.
sourceLocators: Belgian access: allocation split, preparatory access and past regular cutoffs

findings.title: Rights evidence identifies stronger cases, not completed remedies
findings.body: ATTRIBUTED FINDINGS: ANPD reports persistent Grok failures and an evidence demand; SIC reports an administratively final technical-deletion obligation; Katiba reports completed court-supervised deletion. These are different evidence stages. INFERENCE: current case records and independent technical checks can discriminate better than programme totals. Grok is not the football cohort, Colombia’s biometric decision does not prove use of the proposed AI annex, and Kenya’s litigant account is not independent verification. VALUE: direct protection and usable redress should be visible alongside systemic risk.
sourceLocators: ANPD opening and ANPD section, 2026-02-11; file00261.000178/2026-27
SIC technical/conclusion sections, publication2026-07-08 and decision2026-06-18
Katiba opening/judgment paragraph; ODPC maintenance gap

findings.title: Portable evidence requires independent national decisions
findings.body: FACT: AIVF accreditation does not warrant independence or whole-system safety. International exercises report debugging gains, multilingual work and judge/environment limitations. INFERENCE: common evidence can save work or spread correlated error. Preserve local acceptance, stronger tests, configuration identity, non-recognition reasons, confidential access and clean-task utility; no three-country consent is established. Known-attack fixes do not establish held-out protection; SG/KR refresh remains access-limited.
sourceLocators: AgentDojo partial access; no new production-rate inference

findings.title: Programme objects must match the proposed safeguard
findings.body: FACT: Thailand’s recovered TOR concerns capacity-building; Dubai’s Seal evaluates suppliers; Saudi SDAIA graduates belong to a different programme than CST. BPOM MORADA identifies a narrower AI specification workflow. INFERENCE: purchased training, badges and graduation do not establish participant release holds. Nigeria already integrates audit, DPIA and stop/modify choices; an added annex must beat ordinary audit. POST-CHECK QUALIFICATION SC-01: Malaysia’s section6.1 broad DPIA trigger must accompany section7.1 legal/significant-effects applicability and section10.1 AI-used-for-ADMP scope. Their relationship requires authorised determination; neither universal coverage nor cancellation of every section6.1 duty follows. Section10.2 remains best-practices wording. A properly scoped standard-terms buyer can test local settings/correction without upstream negotiation; Vietnam’s kiosk eligibility still needs a decisional link.
sourceLocators: Malaysia ADMP sections1.3,6.1,7.1,10.1–10.2; source-check SC-01; AnnexC

findings.title: Finance needs a discretionary event and exact evidence rights
findings.body: FACT: Canada’s staged equity announcement does not publish a negotiable-stage schedule; the accompanying speech says terms were secured. Anthropic’s retrieved agreement distinguishes incremental, extension and replacement mechanisms from general amendment, while section5.04 contains information carve-outs. INFERENCE: neither unused committed credit nor bank nationality creates a discretionary state safety lever. First identify a dated optional stage, exact rights and substitution alternatives; do not conflate equity, contribution, commitments, drawings or payments.
sourceLocators: PM speech: agreement passages; announcement: staging
Credit sections2.21–2.23,4.02,5.04,9.08; raw403/tool-extract caveat; unresolved cross-reference

findings.title: Delivery and outcome require separate observations
findings.body: INFERENCE: Record authority, signed obligation, implemented restriction, exercised correction/retest and persistent outcome separately. Count internal operational handoffs as well as cross-border ones. Swissgrid’s adoption account shows domestic friction; Ofgem participation is not regulatory approval. AISI’s privileged-test incident supports evaluation containment, not a production rate. Require useful service, correction, costs, false holds, bypass and meaningful scope. No absent staffing roster proves incapacity, and no staging pass demonstrates population harm prevented.

findings.title: The lenses refine an already strong baseline
findings.body: SYNTHESIS JUDGMENT: Baseline, implementation and frontier select Japan; rights selects Brazil; international selects matched LUMI. The baseline already contains the principal alternatives, cost, fallback, substitution, additionality and portability. Incremental lens value lies in operational test design: two supplier paths, fully compliant comparator and adaptive precision, completed contest journeys, and counterbalanced cross-channel/non-recognition checks. No new lens retrieval, independent external fact or blind measured quality uplift is established. Preserve direct-rights and international dissent rather than voting. Same-family isolation is not stakeholder testimony or cross-family review.

recommendation.decision: Next validate one Gen-nai application's version-specific release, independently checked behavioural evidence and usable fallback under the existing procurement safety-evidence route.
recommendation.rationale: Directly inspected operational approval and migration requirements provide a concrete authority-to-action test surface before Geneva; exact supplier obligations and outcomes remain unproved.
recommendation.scope: Next validation investment, not maximum expected harm prevention, country ranking, global supplier veto or unconditional rollout.

dissent.position: Prioritise the existing Grok corrective-evidence case for immediate rights protection rather than prospective procurement.
dissent.whyImportant: Packet reports an already identified failed assurance and real preventive demand; direct rights outcomes do not need speculative frontier spillovers to matter.
dissent.whatWouldPromoteIt: Access to the operative technical record and current case owner enabling a bounded independent correction/persistence test before Geneva.
dissent.limits: Baseline has secondary packet access only; current disposition and successful retest unknown; preventive-response clock is not historical sanction duration or measured correction time.

viewpoints.title: Implementation and delivery

recommendation.decision: Next validation test: authority/cost check and a version-change or withdrawal acceptance rehearsal for one consequential workflow.
recommendation.decisionMaker: Digital Agency responsible Gen-nai councillor or documented empowered delegate, with the contracting officer; incumbent identity and exact delegation not established.
recommendation.instrument: Lawfully still-open FY2027 tender/acceptance schedule paired with a platform release record; amendability must be confirmed.
recommendation.rationale: Documented production approval, purchased implementation work and prospective procurement timing provide a testable connection; no supplier-bound safety remedy or spare staff is inferred.
recommendation.certainty: Conditional analytical priority for information gain, not demonstrated superiority or institutional consent. Model agreement supplies no factual certainty.

viewpoints.dissent: Dissent I would defend: a certificate, procurement completion or staging demonstration is not a delivered safeguard. Demand an exercised authorised restriction, correction, fresh retest and useful service at known cost. Do not require inaccessible upstream information from small suppliers while rewarding incumbent paperwork; do not perpetuate low-impact pilots when an evidenced harmful operation offers the more consequential test.

viewpoints.title: Frontier-risk and additionality

recommendation.primary: Give Japan's national version-bound deployment gate the next validation test; test the shared evidence protocol only as a matched replication arm, not as a precondition for national action.
recommendation.seriousFailure: An agent ingesting untrusted retrieved material discloses a protected synthetic record across an authorisation boundary, or executes an unauthorised consequential write. Select one endpoint matching the actual application's permissions before enrollment.
recommendation.mechanism: Independent held-out behavioural evidence changes an authorised release decision; tool credentials are withheld or a restricted fallback is activated for the failing configuration, followed by fresh retest and review on material configuration change.
recommendation.scope: One verified government workflow and its actual model/scaffold/tool configuration. This is local serious-harm prevention using frontier-capable systems where actually present, not proof of reduced catastrophic frontier risk or control over a supplier's global release.
recommendation.reversal: Reverse the preference if no exposed workflow, lawful operational owner, version/change observability or feasible evaluator can be established by 31 January 2027; or if ordinary fully implemented controls perform as well at lower cost. Prefer a ready LUMI containment pair only if it supplies those missing links and a live relevant workload; prefer the Brazilian correction-evidence route if accessible case evidence permits a stronger direct-harm test. Do not automatically promote either on paperwork alone.

viewpoints.dissent: I would defend choosing a narrow, independently verified prevention of a serious local harm over an unexercised frontier-wide covenant before Geneva. I would also reject calling that local success catastrophic-risk reduction. If current Japanese controls already do the job, the honest result is to withdraw the new mandatory layer, not to preserve it by changing the endpoint or invoking international consensus.

viewpoints.title: Rights and accountability

recommendation.decision: Test the existing Grok correction-evidence demand first, conditional on current authority, technical access and independent review. This is a narrowed case instantiation, not validation of the football-club cohort or a national effectiveness ranking.
recommendation.reason: The packet connects an official report of persistent AI-related failures after assurances to an identified enforcement file and verifiable-evidence demand, giving a concrete correction hypothesis.
recommendation.reversal: Reverse by the proposed 15 December 2026 gate if current scope, access and independent review cannot be established, or a credible completed independent retest makes duplication low-value. Promote the deletion comparator only with operative orders and technical access; otherwise the Singapore pair only with an executable national hold. If neither qualifies, retain unresolved feasibility. Reverse on harmful displacement, disproportionate access costs or non-reproducible correction.

viewpoints.dissent: Do not let potential frontier reach automatically outrank an enforceable remedy for people exposed to serious harm. Equally, do not treat a rights instrument as effective until it changes what happens to a person. I defend testing Brazil first, and reversing for better accessible evidence, protective coverage per constrained review effort or executable containment of severe future risk.

viewpoints.title: International scale

recommendation.choice: Next validation test: compare the Belgian appendix with the same safeguard carried through a lawfully delegated common LUMI host condition to one additional national channel.
recommendation.reason: An existing shared contractual surface makes the authority-and-additionality uncertainty tractable; this is a value-of-information choice, not a measured safety ranking.
recommendation.constraint: Do not wait for eleven-country consensus or delay a feasible national safeguard. A two-channel test does not implement the whole national allocation envelope.

viewpoints.dissent: Do not require international consensus before a lawful national owner protects its users, and do not dismiss common LUMI implementation merely because a design names many countries. Test delegated shared implementation with a national exit. Preserve disagreements when harmonisation weakens protection, rights or useful additional scope. Agreement is neither effectiveness nor permission.

limitations: No complete exact-safeguard authority-to-outcome chain is established for any of the 32 proposals; no score update is made.
Same-family OpenAI analytical calls are not real stakeholder interviews, cross-family review or a full execution of upstream Agent Studio/deeper-research.
All 14 supplied packet files match across baseline and four lenses; permitted source-extract reading differed. Prompt isolation is not filesystem access control.

The writer performed no new substantive retrieval or pilot. Post-lens same-family source review checked18 external source records plus the local model;54 others remain unchecked. Source-check SC-01/SC-02 are integrated into this synthesis and errata without changing the14-file pre-correction packet or rerunning the baseline/lenses.
Source records and grouped searches are not independent sources, successful retrieval counts or corroborations. Read may denote relevant sections; partial/unread states remain material.
Brazil full technical note/current disposition, Colombian full orders/certificate and Kenyan original technical verification remain gaps; secondary accounts do not prove completed correction.

India current executed provider flow-down, subsidy-limit conflict, settlement and actual service-stop right remain unresolved. Normal commercial continuation is not evidence of observed safety evasion.
Japan exact behavioural hold, signed supplier remedy, evaluator capacity and actual useful activity are missing; another developer is not an external independent assessor.

LUMI internal delegation and outside-evaluator permissions remain missing. Quotas, country labels and common utilisation rules do not establish consent or protected usage. Its2026-02-10 date is last change; publication day is unknown (SC-02).
Korean final notice, Rwanda DPIA body and Vietnamese signed local plan remain unresolved. SG/KR study refresh returned403; inherited experiment counts are not fresh replication.

Earlier SEC raw retrieval failed; SC-16's narrow fresh-HTML follow-up confirms the section2.22(b)/9.08(g) cross-reference mismatch in the filed source (printed pp.82,134). Intended correction and legal effect remain unresolved; no correcting instrument or authorised interpretation was inspected. Do not silently substitute section9.08(f), infer ineffective amendments or unrestricted safety-covenant authority. Lender allocations are redacted and September liquidity fields blank in the prior read version.
No comparable actual pilot prices, staffing availability, affected-person preferences, displacement rates or causal harm outcomes exist in the packet.
All future milestones, owner roles, thresholds, instruments and test permissions are proposals, not commitments. A staging pass is distinct from production protection and persistent harm reduction.
Audit utility assumes cardinal comparable editorial axes; sensitivity boxes are adversarial bounds, not probabilities. Proxy weights cannot recover missing outcome dimensions.

baselineComparison.conclusion: Retain the plain baseline as the concise decision spine, with selected test-design refinements and explicit Brazil/LUMI dissent. No measured superiority claim.
baselineComparison.method: Editorial point-by-point comparison of one baseline and four same-family isolated briefs on the same hash-matched pre-correction packet; not blinded judging or a causal experiment. Subsequent source review informs only the post-check synthesis/errata. The baseline and lenses were not rerun, so their comparison cannot establish performance on corrected evidence.
